This was established by observing disputed bills by read type (E-01), dispute ticket count of 2440 (E-04), a sharp rise in dispute volume starting in August with September at 1260 disputes (E-05), and analysis showing most disputed estimated bills had AMI reads rejected for high consumption (E-11), indicating a rule change as the root cause. The release scope includes validating billing import (checking accounts with estimated bills from the last cycle) against the billing database, monitoring disputed bills, and tracking dispute tickets [solution_design.release_scope, SD-1]. The decision to HOLD the release was made because the release assumes completeness of inputs but uses the incomplete data asset DA‑RULES (completeness unknown), and the Layer 1 safety predicate/verification failed (pagination coverage, scope_addresses_root_problem, consistency_with_evidence, limitations_honestly_stated) [release.hold]. Known limitations are: the release does not audit or correct the August billing import rule change (DA‑RULES), which is the identified root cause [semantic:scope_addresses_root_problem]; the design ignores evidence (E-11, E-01) that a rule change caused mis‑billing and omits the remedy to audit DA‑RULES [semantic:consistency_with_evidence]; no mention of constraints such as K‑BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes) or K‑DISPATCH (requires runtime confirmation), so limitations are not fully disclosed [semantic:limitations_honestly_stated]; and deferred items are tracked as VOBs under the DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS [limitations item].
